host_side_venv.why: the 13 failures are all numpy_unavailable. Those tests exercise capture/gate paths that are IN-IMAGE by design; the host driver venv has no numpy and must not have one - installing numpy on the host would introduce versions different from the image the tests compare against, which would make a pass meaningless.

why_the_thread_count_hazard_did_not_mate: The owner concern - more vCPUs changing thread counts, BLAS behaviour, or affinity - is the hazard the frozen threading policy already addresses, and the custody code ENFORCES it rather than assuming it: _require_frozen_threading() REFUSES to capture when any of OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS or OPENBLAS_CORETYPE is unset, on the stated grounds that an unset variable takes a library default that is a function of the host core count. All five were set to the frozen values for this capture, OpenBLAS is built NO_AFFINITY, and OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=HASWELL pins kernel dispatch independently of the detected CPU. threading_policy_branch remains FROZEN; the alternative branch (proving that varying the thread variables leaves governed output hashes unchanged) is still NOT performed and is not relied on here.
